arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Thu: a call she took on the street ('administrative stuff'), then 'I'll answer by December' at the counter, one leaf, a coffee for the road. He wrote 'I want to talk to Dana' in the notebook. The Moshe photo is due Sat Nov 14, after havdalah.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Thu: three 'small things' in one day (the rolling chickpea, a pastel header, more tweaks at 23:05), every time 'we'll settle it all together'. Fri: Ishai asks for a payment date in writing; behind Gadi's hand, another freelancer is waiting too.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Thu: cancelled the bar, came anyway, left early, ignored Shir's calls ('just Shir'), turned up at his door at ten 'not ready'. Fri: says yes to Shabbat dinner, almost says 'Shir and I', then cancels at candle time.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 2 done Thu Nov 12 (gifts, 'I want'). Homework: one 'I want' to someone who matters; the notebook says 'I want to talk to Dana'. Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Thu: the cough ('the weather'), Ishai took the cats' bowl down and promised tea. Fri: lemon and honey tea; she says Eli calls every Friday at eight. He doesn't; she comes over with 'too much soup' for Shabbat dinner and says his battery died.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Thu: Ishai overheard 'Double? From January? Thirty years I'm here...'; Avi said chickpeas and lost his proverb. Ishai paid full price.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Thu: asked Ishai the 'hypothetical' about someone you like leaving town and wrote down his answer ('have a nice trip, to a cup').
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Thu: went very quiet when Noa burst into the bar, then pretended a napkin with a name on it was nothing. Next: the Pump House gallery night Wed Nov 18 with Ishai.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

beats.goal: Friday morning at the desk. Gadi phones: Ruti loves last night's tweaks. Ishai tries his improv homework and says 'I want' to Gadi: a payment date, in writing. Gadi jokes it away ('a date, like a wedding'), says December 8th 'is in the system', then muffles the phone and tells someone in his office 'tell Ofer Monday, I said Monday'. Ishai half hears it and lets it go. Never say Gadi is in trouble.
beats.teaser: Ishai tries his improv homework on Gadi: 'I want...'
beats.forceText: Gadi phones about the tweaks; Ishai asks him for a payment date in writing and Gadi laughs it off.

forceLines.say: Gadi, I want a date. For the payment. In writing.
A date! Like a wedding. December eighth, habibi, it's in the system.

forceCommentary.say: He said 'I want' to Gadi. Before nine. On a Friday. Who IS this man?

moments.text: Friday morning, coffee by the laptop, the YES, AND notebook open next to it. Gadi calls; Ishai answers standing, then sits, then stands again.

lines.say: Ishai! The tweaks! Ruti says the chickpea rolls like it means it.
Good. Great. So that's the last one? For the app?
The last one. Probably. Ninety percent. Clients, you know.
Gadi, I want... I want a date. For the payment.
A date! Like a wedding? I'll bring flowers.
In writing. An email. Just the day it lands.
December eighth, thirty days, it's in the system. You know me.
I do. That's why I want it in writing.
Ooh. Look at you. Who taught you that?
A woman with a notebook. Long story. So, the email?

commentary.say: He said 'I want' to Gadi. Before nine. On a Friday. I'm shaking.
'You know me.' The three scariest words in freelance.

moments.text: Gadi covers the phone badly; a muffled voice in his office, then his own, sharper than usual. Ishai frowns at the speaker.

lines.say: One second. ...Tell Ofer Monday. I said Monday! Close the door.
Gadi? Everything okay over there?
Fine! The printer guy. Printers. Always want something.
Sounds like he wants Monday.
Everybody wants Monday. Monday is very popular this year.
So I'll get the email today?
Today, tomorrow, Sunday. Shabbat shalom, my prince. Small change!
It's not small change. It's five and a half thousand.
Exactly, small change for a big talent. Bye bye bye.
Bye. ...He hung up. Of course he hung up.

commentary.say: 'Tell Ofer Monday.' I'd like to know what Ofer's invoice says.
'Small change' is not a payment method, Gadi. I checked.

update.memory: Ishai asked for a payment date in writing. First time ever. Told him December 8th. He heard me tell someone about Ofer. Printers, I said.

moments.text: Ishai sits back at the desk, opens the notebook and under 'I want to talk to Dana' writes a second line, slowly.

lines.say: 'I want a date.' Payment kind. Not the other kind. Yet.

commentary.say: Two lines in the notebook now. Somebody's growing.
Note there is still no email from Gadi. I'm keeping count.

beats.goal: Shabbat shopping at Shuk Shalom (it closes at 14:00 on Fridays): challah, vegetables, and lemons, ginger and honey for Mrs. Levi's cough. From the market Ishai phones Noa to invite her to Shabbat dinner. She says yes too fast and too bright, starts to say 'Shir and I' and changes it to 'just me'. Ishai sends Shabbat shalom to Shir; Noa goes quiet for a second. He notices nothing. Never say Shir moved out.
beats.teaser: Ishai invites Noa for Shabbat dinner, and she says yes
beats.forceText: At Shuk Shalom Ishai buys challah and lemons for Mrs. Levi and phones Noa, who says yes to Shabbat dinner.

forceLines.say: Shabbat dinner tonight? Eight. I'm buying too much challah anyway.
Yes! Yes. Eight. I'll bring wine. Just me.

forceCommentary.say: 'Just me.' She said it like she'd practised it.

moments.text: Shuk Shalom on a Friday morning, loud and crowded. Ishai holds a bag of lemons, a knob of ginger and a jar of honey up to his face, reading the jar's label like a contract.

lines.say: Lemon, honey, hot water, not boiling. Not boiling. Got it, Mrs. Levi.
And one challah. Two. Two is Shabbat.

commentary.say: He's buying cough supplies for his neighbour. I'm not crying, it's the spice stall.
Reading a honey label for nine seconds. That's a man who has been burned by honey before.

moments.text: By the juice stall, two challahs under one arm, Ishai calls Noa. She answers on the first ring, very awake, very cheerful.

lines.say: Hey. Shabbat dinner tonight? Eight. I bought too much challah.
Yes! Yes. Eight. Amazing. I'll bring wine. Shir and I... just me. I'll bring wine.
Just you? Shir's working?
Shir's... busy. Very busy. You know Shir.
Tell her Shabbat shalom from me. And from Falafel.
I'll... yes. I'll tell her. Sure.
You okay? You said yes five times.
I'm great. I'm hungry. Last night I was weird, forget last night.
I only remember the part where you came anyway.
Good. Keep that part. What are you cooking?
Something with lemon. Mrs. Levi's got a cough, I'm on lemon duty.
Of course you are. Eight. Don't apologise when I walk in.

commentary.say: 'Shir and I... just me.' Somebody edited that sentence live.
Five yeses. FIVE. Noa, blink twice if you need a hug.

update.memory: Said yes to Shabbat dinner at Ishai's, eight. Almost said 'Shir and I'. He sent Shir Shabbat shalom. I said I'd tell her.

beats.goal: Ishai brings Mrs. Levi the lemon, ginger and honey tea he promised (not boiling) in the corridor, and invites her to Shabbat dinner. She coughs, refuses: her son Eli calls every Friday at eight, 'eight sharp'. Then Moti comes up the stairs with the committee notebook; when Ishai mentions Eli's Friday call, Moti goes quiet for a beat and changes the subject to the cats and the cough. Never say Eli hasn't visited.
beats.teaser: Mrs. Levi turns down Shabbat dinner: Eli calls at eight
beats.forceText: Ishai brings Mrs. Levi lemon and honey tea and invites her for Shabbat dinner; she says Eli calls every Friday at eight.

forceLines.say: Thank you, motek. But Friday at eight, Eli calls. Eight sharp.
Then come after. The soup will wait.

forceCommentary.say: Eight sharp, she says. Write that down, people.

moments.text: The corridor. Ishai knocks at Mrs. Levi's door holding a mug with a saucer on top; she opens in her cardigan and coughs into her sleeve before she says hello.

lines.say: Lemon, ginger, honey. Not boiling. I checked twice.
Ginger? I didn't say ginger.
The man at the market said ginger. He was very sure.
Market men are always sure. ...Mm. It's good. Don't tell him.
Come for Shabbat dinner tonight. Noa's coming. Eight o'clock.
Eight? No, motek. Friday at eight Eli calls. Eight sharp. Every week.
Then come after the call. Bring him on speaker.
He talks a long time. Big company, many stories.
The door's open all night. Well, till eleven.
Go cook. And put a coat on that dog, it's November.

commentary.say: Ginger. He went off-script with the ginger. Growth.
Eli calls 'eight sharp, every week'. I've heard that tone before. From my basil.

update.memory: Ishai brought lemon tea with ginger, not boiling. Invited me for Shabbat dinner. Told him Eli calls Fridays at eight, sharp.

moments.text: Moti comes up the stairs with the committee notebook under his arm as Mrs. Levi's door closes. He looks at the closed door, then at Ishai.

lines.say: Apartment four. Delivering soup now? The committee approves.
Tea. For her cough. She won't come to dinner, Eli calls at eight.
Eli calls. ...Yes. Good. That's good.
You know him? Her son?
I knew him at twelve. He broke the stair light with a football.
So it's been broken since the nineties. That explains Tomer's tape.
Listen. The walls are thin. If the cough gets worse, you hear it first.
I'll listen. I'm good at that. Ask anyone.
And the cats. If she can't go down, the cats don't care about coughs.
Bowl at the kiosk, one o'clock. The orange one doesn't trust me yet.

commentary.say: Moti said 'that's good' like a man reading a sad receipt.
The committee has feelings. Mark the date.

update.memory: Ishai brought Mrs. Levi tea and says Eli calls Fridays at eight. Didn't tell him. Asked him to listen for her cough and feed the cats.

beats.goal: The table is set for two, the challahs under a cloth. Just before candle lighting (16:22) Noa texts that she can't come after all ('something came up'). Ishai lights the two Shabbat candles alone by the window, next to Moshe and the sprout, Falafel watching.
beats.teaser: Shabbat candles at 16:22, and a text Ishai didn't expect
beats.forceText: Noa cancels Shabbat dinner by text; Ishai lights the Shabbat candles alone by the window.

forceLines.say: 'Something came up.' On Shabbat. Okay. Shabbat shalom, Moshe.

forceCommentary.say: A table for two, and one of them is a basil.

moments.text: Two plates, two glasses, the challahs under a cloth. Ishai's phone buzzes on the table; he reads it standing, a match box still in his hand.

message.say: Can't tonight after all. Something came up. So sorry. Save me challah? Shabbat shalom

lines.say: 'Something came up.' On Shabbat. At four. Okay.
Save you challah. I bought two, Noa. Two.

commentary.say: Cancelled. By text. Six minutes to candles. Noa, honey, what is GOING on?
Two challahs, one man. That's not dinner, that's a bakery.

moments.text: At the window Ishai lights the two candles, circles his hands over them three times and covers his eyes; Moshe and the little sprout stand in the glow, Falafel sits very still.

lines.say: Shabbat shalom, Moshe. Shabbat shalom, roommate. You too, Falafel.

commentary.say: Moshe, lit by candlelight. Finally the lighting he deserves.
He blessed the basil AND the sprout. If that's not a husband, I don't know what is.

beats.goal: Shabbat evening. Around half past seven Mrs. Levi knocks with a pot of soup ('I made too much, by accident'): Eli's phone battery died, he'll call Sunday. Ishai doesn't ask more; he sets Noa's plate for her. Kiddush, soup, her cough, stories of Eli as a boy. She sees the open notebook ('I want to talk to Dana') and tells him to send the basil girl the photo. She goes home before eleven. Never say Eli hasn't visited.
beats.teaser: A knock on Shabbat evening, with a pot of soup
beats.forceText: Mrs. Levi comes over with soup for Shabbat dinner; Eli's battery died, she says. She tells Ishai to send the girl the basil photo.

forceLines.say: His battery died. These phones. He'll call Sunday.
Then you're just in time. Noa's plate is free.

forceCommentary.say: Nobody's battery dies at exactly eight, Mrs. Levi. Nobody's.

moments.text: A knock. Mrs. Levi in a coat over her cardigan, holding a pot with both hands and a challah balanced on the lid.

lines.say: I made too much soup. By accident. For two. Don't ask how.
Mrs. Levi! Did Eli call?
His battery died. These phones. He'll call Sunday.
Then you're just in time. Noa's plate is free.
She didn't come? A girl doesn't come to Shabbat?
Something came up. Sit. The good chair, by the candles.
Who taught you to set a table? Forks on the left, good.
You did. Last year. You said I eat like a student.
You still eat like a student. Bring bowls.

commentary.say: Nobody's battery dies at exactly eight, Mrs. Levi. Nobody's.
Too much soup 'by accident'. Soup is never an accident.

moments.text: Ishai says kiddush over a small cup of wine, a little fast; they tear the challah and eat her soup. She coughs between spoonfuls and waves away his worry.

lines.say: Faster than my husband, slower than the rabbi. Acceptable.
I practised in the shower. Is the soup chicken or a miracle?
Chicken. The miracle is the dill. Eli hated dill.
What was he like? As a kid?
He drew on my walls. A whole bus, on the kitchen wall. In pen.
Did you paint over it?
Never. It's still there. Behind the fridge.
That's a designer. Draws on walls, nobody pays him.
Like you. Eat. You're thin and you cough at nothing.
You're the one coughing.
Mine is the weather. Yours is worry. Different department.

commentary.say: A bus in pen, behind the fridge, kept for years. I need to lie down.
'Different department.' She's diagnosing him now. Iconic.

moments.text: Clearing the bowls, Mrs. Levi spots the YES, AND notebook open on the desk and reads it without asking, glasses down her nose.

lines.say: 'I want to talk to Dana.' Who is Dana?
That's... homework. Private homework.
The coffee girl. With the basil. The whole building knows, motek.
The whole building? How?
Moti. Avi. The cats. So talk to her.
Tomorrow I'm sending her a photo of Moshe. After havdalah.
A photo of a plant. That's your move?
She asked for it. It's a whole... it's a thing between us.
Then send it. And write something. Not 'sorry'.
What should I write?
What you want. It's in your book already. Goodnight, Shabbat shalom.

commentary.say: Mrs. Levi just read his diary out loud and I've never loved her more.
'Not sorry.' Pin that to his forehead.

update.memory: Shabbat dinner at Ishai's with my soup. Told him Eli's battery died. He didn't ask. Read his notebook: Dana. Told him to send the photo, not 'sorry'.

moments.text: Alone, the candles burnt low, Ishai opens the photo of Moshe and the sprout on his phone, holds his thumb over Dana's name, then turns the phone face down. It's Shabbat.

lines.say: Tomorrow. After three stars. Not sorry. Something good.

commentary.say: His thumb was RIGHT THERE. Tomorrow, Ishai. I'm holding you to it.
Three stars. That's also my rating for this cliffhanger.

hook.text: Eli's battery 'died' at eight. And tomorrow after havdalah: will Ishai finally send Dana the photo, and what will he write?

previously.text: Noa cancelled the bar, came anyway, left early and turned up at Ishai's door at ten: 'I'm not ready.' In his notebook: 'I want to talk to Dana.'

hosts: Friday in Tel Aviv: half the city is cooking, the other half is pretending they didn't forget challah.
Shabbat starts at 16:22 today. Ishai has never once been ready at 16:21.
Gadi's 'small things' this week: three. Gadi's payments this week: let's not.
Ishai's notebook now has one full sentence in it. That's a library by his standards.
Moshe update: eight leaves, one roommate, zero complaints.
Reminder: the Moshe photo is due tomorrow. Dana asked twice. Ishai set two reminders.
Mrs. Levi's cough is 'the weather'. The weather has been clear for three days.
Noa said 'I'm perfect' last night. Nobody perfect says it twice.
Who calls a barista about 'administrative stuff' at ten in the morning? Asking for Zohar.
Lior typed faster every time Dana walked past yesterday. Writers are not subtle people.
Avi said chickpeas doubled. I checked. Chickpeas are fine. Avi is not.
Tomer went very quiet when Noa walked into the bar. Tomer is never quiet. Never.
Falafel has walked more this week than Gadi has paid. Good boy.
If you're new: Ishai is a designer, Falafel is a husky-ish, Moshe is a basil, and we are unwell.
Market run today. Watch Ishai pick a lemon like it's a job interview.
Friday flowers on Herzl Street. Ishai will walk past them. He always walks past them.
Oren's prediction: Gadi says 'small change' at least once before noon.
Zohar's prediction: the word 'Dana' gets said in that apartment tonight. Write it down.
Two challahs is a statement. One challah is a lifestyle.
Next week: improv lesson three, a gallery night at the Pump House, and our nerves.
Somebody in this building knows more than they're saying. Several somebodies, actually.
Kiddush speed rating so far this season: Ishai, fast. Very fast. Olympic.
Noa's phone keeps lighting up with the same name. She keeps turning it over. Just saying.
Dear Ishai: 'I want' is two words. You need a third one. Love, Zohar.
Oren's basil corner: Moshe is not ready for a relationship. He's focusing on himself.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Friday morning, and the whole city smells like onions frying for tonight.
Thirteen degrees and clear. Bring a jacket, take it off at noon, lose it by two.
The market closes at two today. If you're still in bed, the good tomatoes are already gone.
A listener asks if it's rude to bring store-bought dessert to Shabbat dinner. Yes. Bring it anyway.
Candle lighting in Tel Aviv at 16:22. In Jerusalem earlier, because Jerusalem likes to win.
Our traffic report: everyone is driving to their mother's. Good luck.
A caller says her husband apologises to the GPS. Ma'am, we have a whole show about men like that.
Song requests this morning are all slow. It's Friday. The city is tired and in love.
Fun fact: honey never goes bad. Unlike my ex's playlists.
If someone made too much soup for you this week, call them. That's the whole message.
Next hour: songs about weekends that never quite arrive.
Radio Herzl 88.2: we close early on Fridays too, but in spirit only.

zelig: The pigeons know it's Friday. They always know.
Too much bread in this park on Fridays. Everybody's sorry for something.
A man who brings tea to a neighbour, that's a man. I told the duck.
Toldot. Two brothers, one blessing. Same old story.
michal: Run club at seven. I came at seven-forty. That counts.
Friday reps. Nobody's here. The mirror is all mine.
He didn't come to run club. Neither did I. Respect.
sivan: Friday pace is a lie. Everyone slows down for chicken soup.
Thirteen minutes and the guy with the husky isn't here. Weak.
lior: Chapter four: the man buys two challahs for one dinner. No, too sad. Keep it.
Fridays she leaves early. Fridays I write slower.
Hypothetically, a person could leave a city. Hypothetically, a person could cry about it in a cafe.
kobi: Friday night, the system says red. The system is always red on Fridays.
Shabbat shalom to everyone except the lottery.
One more and I'll tell you about the scooter. Again.
My mother used to light candles. I light the jukebox.

street: ...I told her the flowers were for my mother, technically they were...
...no, the kiosk is open, Avi's always open, he looked tired though...
...fifteen minutes to candles and he's buying batteries...
...my aunt calls it 'soup weather' when it's thirteen degrees...
market: ...two kilos of tomatoes for four people, are you feeding an army...
...the honey man said it fixes everything, I said even my landlord...
...last challah, last challah, sesame or plain, decide...
...she's coming for dinner, so I'm buying the expensive lemons...
park: ...Friday is the only day the joggers say hello back...
...he feeds the pigeons like they owe him money...
...my son said he'll call tonight, he says that every week...
cafe: ...she said Haifa, or she said I'm hungry, it was loud...
...two shots, oat, and do you do Shabbat takeaway...
...he writes the same page every day, I think he's in love with it...

chat.say: Reminder: stairwell light works again thanks to Tomer. Please do not test it with footballs.
Anyone have a spare candle? Mine are birthday ones. They're shaped like 3 and 0.
Apt 7, I have plain ones. Knock. Not before ten, I'm coughing.
Whoever parks the scooter by the bins, the bins have feelings too.
The 88 runs until 15:30 today. After that you walk, like our ancestors.
Mrs. Levi's cats will be fed at one by apartment four. Thank you apartment four.
The cats don't need a committee announcement. But thank you.
Shabbat shalom everyone. My candles are still a 3 and a 0. God understands.
Shabbat shalom. Quiet hours from candle lighting. Yes, Apt 7, that means you too.
